fmt_tbl <- function(df, right = NULL, caption = NULL) {
  right_cols <- union(names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, TRUE)], right)
  left_cols <- setdiff(names(df), right_cols)
  ft <- flextable::flextable(df)
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, align = "center", part = "header")
  if (length(right_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = right_cols, align = "right", part = "body")
  if (length(left_cols)) ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = left_cols, align = "left", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::line_spacing(ft, space = 1, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::padding(ft, padding.top = 1, padding.bottom = 1,part = "all")

frame_at_scale <- function(x, scale, width_in, height_in, crs = "EPSG:32605") {
  bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(x, crs))
  cx <- mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]); cy <- mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")])
  hw <- width_in  * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  hh <- height_in * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - hw, ymin = cy - hh, xmax = cx + hw, ymax = cy + hh),
              crs = sf::st_crs(crs))
}

# Abstract

```{r}
#| label: abstract-numbers
#| echo: true
#| output: false
acc_csv <- "03.outputs/accuracy.csv"; pred_csv <- "03.outputs/tile_predictions.csv"
stopifnot(file.mtime(acc_csv) >= file.mtime(pred_csv))  # the accuracy chunk below rewrote it from the same predictions
summ <- read.csv(acc_csv); net <- summ[summ$method == "TempCNN" & summ$set == "training", ]
n_cells <- nrow(read.csv("02.inputs/derived/tile_cells.csv"))
```

Sentinel-1 radar records the boreal forest through cloud at a 12-day repeat, and whether that record can map spruce beetle mortality that Landsat change analysis misses below a stand severity of 0.1 has not been tested on areas held out from training. This study trained a temporal convolutional network on the slope-corrected Sentinel-1 record of June 2017 to August 2021 at the hand-delineated dead spruce crowns of Zwieback et al. (2024) in the Susitna valley of Southcentral Alaska (57 training areas of 512 m and 121 test areas of 90 m on one WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021, `r format(n_cells, big.mark = ",")` cells of 10 m), with the record composited at monthly, two-monthly, quarterly and half-yearly intervals, and scored it on areas held out by spatial cross-validation in five folds and on the independent test areas. On the held-out folds the F1 score for cells covered by dead crowns over a tenth of their area against cells with no dead crown ran from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(net$F1))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(net$F1))` and the area under the curve from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(net$AUC))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(net$AUC))` across the four intervals, while the mean of a single band over the same 24 months ranked the cells with an area under the curve of up to `r sprintf("%.2f", summ$AUC[summ$method == "One-band mean" & summ$set == "training"])` with no training at all, and moving the window back through the record showed the network classing cells with and without dead crowns as dead in the same windows. The comparison shows that the network learned the land cover mixed into the live class and the season at which its window ended, not the mortality. A design that sets living forest against dead at the stand scale, with a record that begins before the outbreak, is the one on which the monthly question should be tested.

# Introduction

Outbreaks of the spruce beetle, *Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby, 1837), Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae, have recurred in the spruce forests of Southcentral Alaska for centuries, with outbreak extent linked to summer temperature [@Berg_2006]. From 1990 to 2000 an outbreak killed spruce across 1.19 million ha of Alaskan forest, roughly 40 per cent more than the previous 70 years together [@Werner_2006], and a new outbreak under way since about 2016 has spread from the Susitna lowlands toward the Alaska Range [@Zwieback_2024]. Knowing where and when beetles kill spruce is needed for hazard management, for carbon accounting and for understanding how a warming climate changes boreal disturbance [@Hicke_2024], and for the forestry operations that set pheromone traps and remove infested trees around the early June flight of the adult beetle [@Holsten_2001], yet the operational record for Alaska rests on aerial sketch mapping, whose polygons record only what an observer saw that year and understate dispersed low-severity mortality [@Zwieback_2024].

The size of that gap was measured by @Zwieback_2024, who mapped dead spruce at tree scale from 2 m WorldView-2 imagery with a convolutional network and found that "approximately 90% of dead trees pixels were found in low-severity stands" while "a clear relation between SWIR reflectance change and severity only emerging above 0.1 severity" [@Zwieback_2024, p. 412]. Landsat change methods therefore see only the few severe stands, and the authors concluded that "Mapping past and future outbreaks of low severity from Landsat alone will be challenging. The subtle reflectance changes (Fig. 8d) are compounded by data sparsity due to frequent cloud cover, curtailing time series analysis to account for subseasonal variability", naming "synthetic aperture radar" among the data that "hold promise for early-stage infestation and mortality mapping" [@Zwieback_2024, p. 419]. High-resolution mapping fills the gap only with proprietary imagery, statewide change attribution has relied on the same survey perimeters [@Pastick_2018], and occurrence models predict beetle habitat rather than damage [@Zabihi_2021].

Sentinel-1 images through cloud by day and night and has supplied a C-band record over Alaska on a 12-day repeat since 2017. Its backscatter responds to the water content and structure of the canopy [@Ulaby_1987; @Kellndorfer_2022], both of which change as a beetle-killed spruce dries, sheds its needles and loses its fine branches over the years after attack [@Hicke_2024], so the radar carries a signal that accumulates at the pace of the mortality itself. In Bavaria a random forest on Sentinel-1 features explained 83 to 89 per cent of the variance in a tree vitality score back-dated from deadwood polygons [@Hechtl_2025], but that skill was measured on pixels split at random within polygons, so neighbouring pixels sat on both sides of the split, and no study has measured how well the radar separates beetle-killed spruce from living spruce on areas it never saw in training, nor at what compositing interval the separation holds.

Deep learning models that read the whole satellite time series are the candidate method for that test, since one-dimensional convolutional networks classify satellite image time series without handcrafted temporal features [@Pelletier_2019; reviewed by @Miller_2024], and over the boreal forest of eastern Canada TempCNN and Transformer models on annual Landsat subsequences detected and dated partial and progressive disturbances that LandTrendr-based classification missed [@Perbet_2024]. The temporal resolution such a model needs is an open question for radar. Monthly composites resolve the seasonal cycle of freeze, thaw and leaf-out that dominates C-band backscatter in the boreal forest, but they also carry more speckle than a half-yearly composite of the same scenes, and the interval at which detection is most accurate is the interval at which an operational map could be refreshed.

This study trained a temporal convolutional network on the Sentinel-1 record at the crown labels of @Zwieback_2024, with the following objectives:

1. Measure the accuracy with which the network separated 10 m cells holding dead spruce crowns from cells holding none, on areas held out by spatial cross-validation and on the independent test areas of @Zwieback_2024, with the record composited at monthly, two-monthly, quarterly and half-yearly intervals.
2. Report that accuracy by the fraction of each cell covered by dead crowns, to find the lowest fraction at which the radar detected mortality.
3. Reconstruct when the mortality mapped in August 2021 first became detectable, by moving the network's window back through the record month by month, and compare the reconstruction with the aerial detection survey.

# Study area

```{r}
#| label: areas
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Zwieback et al. (2024) dead spruce crown labels, Zenodo https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10569990, CC-BY 4.0.
# The list files name the WorldView-2 image each area was delineated on.
lab_dir <- "02.inputs/zwieback-labels"
areas <- rbind(transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg/list"), colClasses = "character"), set = "training", dir = "gpkg"),
               transform(read.csv(file.path(lab_dir, "gpkg_validation/list_validation"), colClasses = "character"), set = "test", dir = "gpkg_validation"))
areas$year <- ifelse(areas$image == "014782712010_01", 2021L, 2013L)  # the post-outbreak image of 2021-08-02 and the pre-outbreak image of 2013-07-14
read_area <- function(i) lapply(c(extent = "_extent.gpkg", crowns = "_labels.gpkg"), function(s) sf::st_read(file.path(lab_dir, areas$dir[i], paste0(areas$roi[i], s)), quiet = TRUE))
info <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(areas)), read_area)
areas <- sf::st_sf(areas, crowns = sapply(info, function(a) nrow(a$crowns)), geometry = do.call(c, lapply(info, function(a) sf::st_geometry(a$extent))))
cells_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_cells.csv"
if (!file.exists(cells_csv)) write.csv(do.call(rbind, lapply(which(areas$year == 2021), function(i) {  # dead crown cover of each 10 m cell, on the UTM 5N grid
  a <- info[[i]]; b <- sf::st_bbox(a$extent)
  tpl <- terra::rast(xmin = floor(b$xmin / 10) * 10, xmax = ceiling(b$xmax / 10) * 10, ymin = floor(b$ymin / 10) * 10, ymax = ceiling(b$ymax / 10) * 10, resolution = 10, crs = "EPSG:32605")
  f <- if (nrow(a$crowns)) terra::rasterize(terra::vect(a$crowns), tpl, cover = TRUE) else terra::init(tpl, 0); f[is.na(f)] <- 0
  d <- setNames(as.data.frame(f, xy = TRUE), c("x", "y", "dead"))
  data.frame(roi = areas$roi[i], set = areas$set[i], d[sf::st_intersects(sf::st_as_sf(d, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), a$extent, sparse = FALSE)[, 1], ])
})), cells_csv, row.names = FALSE)
cells <- read.csv(cells_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))
used <- areas[areas$year == 2021, ]
```

The study area was the Talkeetna to Byers Lake stretch of the Susitna valley in Southcentral Alaska, between `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymin"])`° N and `r sprintf("%.1f", sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(used, 4326))["ymax"])`° N along the Parks Highway, where @Zwieback_2024 delineated dead spruce crowns on a WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021 (@fig-study). The forest is a boreal mosaic of white spruce (*Picea glauca* (Moench) Voss), black spruce (*P. mariana* (Mill.) Britton et al.), Alaska birch (*Betula neoalaskana* Sarg.) and trembling aspen (*Populus tremuloides* Michx.) with wetlands and treeless floodplains, in which conifer fractions of 10 to 30 per cent predominate, and the outbreak reached it around 2016 and had killed much of the large white spruce by 2021 [@Zwieback_2024]. Within that frame the aerial detection survey mapped spruce beetle damage on `r format(round(sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads[ads$SURVEY_YEAR == 2018, ]))) / 1e4), big.mark = ",")` ha in 2018, the largest area of any year, and on `r format(round(sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads[ads$SURVEY_YEAR == 2020, ]))) / 1e4), big.mark = ",")` ha in 2020, the least of any year.

# Data

## Reference data

The reference data were the dead spruce crown polygons that @Zwieback_2024 delineated by hand to train and test their network, released as an extent and a set of crowns for each of `r sum(areas$set == "training")` training areas of 512 m and `r sum(areas$set == "test")` test areas of 90 m. The areas delineated on the pre-outbreak image of 14 July 2013 hold `r sum(areas$crowns[areas$year == 2013])` crowns between them and were set aside, leaving the `r sum(used$set == "training")` training areas and `r sum(used$set == "test")` test areas delineated on the image of 2 August 2021, which hold `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "training"]), big.mark = ",")` and `r format(sum(used$crowns[used$set == "test"]), big.mark = ",")` crowns. The crowns record where a spruce stood dead on that date and not when it died, and the delineators could not separate species or mortality agent, so a crown is a dead spruce in an area of beetle outbreak rather than a confirmed beetle kill. Each area was divided into 10 m cells on the WGS 84 UTM zone 5N grid of the labels, `r format(nrow(cells), big.mark = ",")` cells in all, and the fraction of each cell covered by dead crowns was computed, so that a cell with a fraction of 0.1 or more, about one crown, was labelled dead and a cell with no crown was labelled alive; the `r format(sum(cells$dead > 0 & cells$dead < 0.1), big.mark = ",")` cells covered only by the edge of a crown took no part in training and are reported as their own class.

## Sentinel-1 data

```{r}
#| label: s1-flatten
#| echo: true
#| output: false
# Sentinel-1 GRD, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/S1_GRD.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_S1_GRD
# Copernicus GLO-30 DEM, Earth Engine COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1.
# https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/COPERNICUS_DEM_GLO30_2024_1
s1 <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/S1_GRD")$filter(ee$Filter$eq("instrumentMode", "IW"))$
  filter(ee$Filter$listContains("transmitterReceiverPolarisation", "VH"))
dem <- ee$ImageCollection("COPERNICUS/DEM/GLO30_2024_1")$select("DEM")$mosaic()
rad <- pi / 180
flatten <- function(img) {  # volume-model slope correction of Vollrath et al. (2020), layover and shadow masked
  theta <- img$select("angle")$multiply(rad)
  phi <- ee$Image$constant(ee$Terrain$aspect(img$select("angle"))$reduceRegion(ee$Reducer$mean(), img$geometry(), 1000)$get("aspect"))$multiply(rad)
  a_r <- ee$Terrain$slope(dem)$multiply(rad)$tan()$multiply(phi$subtract(ee$Terrain$aspect(dem)$multiply(rad))$cos())$atan()
  g0 <- ee$Image$constant(10)$pow(img$select(c("VV", "VH"))$divide(10))$divide(theta$cos())
  corr <- ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$add(a_r)$tan()$divide(ee$Image$constant(pi / 2)$subtract(theta)$tan())
  ee$Image(g0$divide(corr)$focalMean(1.5)$log10()$multiply(10)$updateMask(a_r$lt(theta)$And(a_r$gt(theta$subtract(pi / 2))))$
    copyProperties(img, list("system:time_start", "relativeOrbitNumber_start")))
}
```

Sentinel-1 ground range detected scenes acquired in interferometric wide swath mode with VV and VH polarisation were read in Google Earth Engine [@Gorelick_2017], where each scene had been corrected for thermal noise, radiometrically calibrated, terrain corrected and converted to decibels. Following the analysis-ready data preparation of @Mullissa_2021, the backscatter was normalised for slope with the volume scattering model of @Vollrath_2020, using the Copernicus 30 m digital elevation model in place of the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission, which does not extend north of 60° N, and pixels in layover or radar shadow were masked. Speckle was reduced with a 3 by 3 pixel mean in linear power before conversion back to decibels. The study area is imaged by two relative orbits, the ascending orbit 65 and the descending orbit 131, which view the forest from opposite sides at different incidence angles, so the two were kept apart as separate bands throughout.

# Methods

## Sample extraction

```{r}
#| label: s1-samples
#| echo: true
#| output: false
samp_dir <- "02.inputs/derived/tile_samples"; dir.create(samp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
months <- seq(as.Date("2017-06-01"), as.Date("2021-08-01"), by = "month"); ym <- format(months, "%Y%m"); orbits <- c(65L, 131L)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(used))) {
  out <- file.path(samp_dir, paste0(used$roi[i], ".csv")); if (file.exists(out)) next
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(used$geometry[i], 4326))
  g <- ee$Geometry$Polygon(list(lapply(seq_len(nrow(xy)), function(k) c(xy[k, 1], xy[k, 2])))); col <- s1$filterBounds(g)
  comp <- list()  # the median of the slope-corrected scenes of each orbit in each month
  for (o in orbits) for (m in seq_along(months)) comp[[length(comp) + 1]] <- col$filter(ee$Filter$eq("relativeOrbitNumber_start", o))$
    filterDate(format(months[m]), format(seq(months[m], by = "month", length.out = 2)[2]))$
    map(flatten)$median()$rename(paste0(c("VV", "VH"), o, "_", ym[m]))
  f <- tryCatch(ee$Image$cat(comp)$sample(region = g, scale = 10, projection = "EPSG:32605", geometries = TRUE, dropNulls = FALSE)$getInfo()$features,
                error = function(e) if (grepl("concurren|Too Many Requests|timed out|memory", conditionMessage(e))) NULL else stop(e))
  if (is.null(f)) next  # left for the next pass when Earth Engine refuses the request under load
  p <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(data.frame(t(sapply(f, function(z) unlist(z$geometry$coordinates)))), coords = 1:2, crs = 4326), 32605))
  write.csv(data.frame(roi = used$roi[i], x = round((p[, 1] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5, y = round((p[, 2] - 5) / 10) * 10 + 5,
                       dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(f, function(z) Filter(Negate(is.null), z$properties)))), out, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

For every month from June 2017, the first month in which both orbits imaged the area, to August 2021, the month of the label image, the median slope-corrected backscatter of each orbit and polarisation was composited in Earth Engine and sampled at the centre of every 10 m cell of every label area, on the same UTM zone 5N grid as the labels, giving four bands per cell per month.

## Time series

```{r}
#| label: series
#| echo: true
#| output: false
bands <- paste0(c("VV", "VH"), rep(orbits, each = 2))
samples <- merge(cells, dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(list.files(samp_dir, "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE), read.csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character"))), by = c("roi", "x", "y"))
months_seen <- sapply(orbits, function(o) length(grep(paste0("^VV", o, "_"), names(samples))))
cube <- array(NA_real_, c(nrow(samples), length(ym), length(bands)), list(NULL, ym, bands))
for (b in bands) { has <- intersect(paste0(b, "_", ym), names(samples)); cube[, sub(".*_", "", has), b] <- as.matrix(samples[, has]) }
samples <- cbind(samples[, c("roi", "set", "x", "y", "dead")], setNames(as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(samples[, c("x", "y")], coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605), 4326))), c("lon", "lat")))
gaps <- mean(is.na(cube))
fill <- function(v) if (sum(!is.na(v)) < 2) v else approx(seq_along(v), v, seq_along(v), rule = 2)$y  # linear interpolation across months without a scene
cube <- aperm(apply(cube, c(1, 3), fill), c(2, 1, 3))
complete <- rowSums(is.na(cube)) == 0
window <- 24L; intervals <- c(1L, 2L, 3L, 6L)
series <- function(end, k = 1L, rows = seq_len(nrow(samples))) {  # the 24 months ending in `end`, averaged over blocks of k months
  j <- (match(end, ym) - window + 1):match(end, ym); blocks <- rep(seq_len(window / k), each = k); x <- cube[rows, j, , drop = FALSE]
  if (k > 1) x <- aperm(apply(x, c(1, 3), function(v) tapply(v, blocks, mean)), c(2, 1, 3))
  list(x = x, dates = months[j][!duplicated(blocks)])
}
as_sits <- function(rows, s) {  # a sits sample table, one time series per cell
  tb <- tibble::tibble(longitude = samples$lon[rows], latitude = samples$lat[rows], start_date = s$dates[1], end_date = tail(s$dates, 1),
                       label = ifelse(samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1, "dead", "alive"), cube = "S1",
                       time_series = lapply(seq_along(rows), function(i) tibble::as_tibble(cbind(data.frame(Index = s$dates), s$x[i, , ]))))
  class(tb) <- c("sits", class(tb)); tb
}
```

The sampled months were assembled into one series of `r length(ym)` months and four bands per cell. `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * gaps)` per cent of the monthly values were missing where an orbit acquired no scene in a month, and these were filled by linear interpolation between the neighbouring months of the same band. The network read a window of 24 months ending in August 2021, the month of the labels, at four compositing intervals, monthly, two-monthly, quarterly and half-yearly, the coarser intervals being the mean of the monthly composites in each block of two, three or six months, so that the same 24 months entered every model as 24, 12, 8 or 4 steps.

## Spatial folds

```{r}
#| label: folds
#| echo: true
#| output: false
train <- samples$set == "training"; use <- (samples$dead >= 0.1 | samples$dead == 0) & complete
ctr <- sf::st_as_sf(aggregate(cbind(x, y) ~ roi, samples[train, ], mean), coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32605)
folds <- blockCV::cv_spatial(ctr, k = 5, size = 15000, selection = "random", seed = 20260915, progress = FALSE, report = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
samples$fold <- folds$folds_ids[match(samples$roi, ctr$roi)]
```

Because the cells of one area share its stand and its radar geometry, the `r nrow(ctr)` training areas were dealt to five spatial folds with blockCV [@Valavi_2019] over hexagons 15 km across, and the network of each fold was trained without the areas of that fold and scored on them, so that no cell was scored by a network that had seen its area. The `r sum(used$set == "test")` test areas of @Zwieback_2024 entered no training and were scored by a network trained on all `r nrow(ctr)` training areas.

## Neural network

```{r}
#| label: tempcnn
#| echo: true
#| output: false
pred_csv <- "03.outputs/tile_predictions.csv"; timing_csv <- "03.outputs/detection_timing.csv"
fit <- function(rows, s) {  # TempCNN of Pelletier et al. (2019) as implemented in sits, on at most 10,000 cells per class
  set.seed(20260915); rows <- unlist(lapply(split(rows, samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1), function(r) r[sample(length(r), min(length(r), 10000))]))
  sits::sits_train(as_sits(rows, s), sits::sits_tempcnn(epochs = 60L, patience = 10L, seed = 20260915L, verbose = FALSE))
}
p_dead <- function(m, rows, s) sapply(sits::sits_classify(as_sits(rows, s), m, multicores = 1L, progress = FALSE)$predicted, function(z) z$dead)
score_rows <- function(m, rows, s, k) data.frame(samples[rows, c("roi", "set", "x", "y", "dead", "fold")], interval = k, p_dead = p_dead(m, rows, s))
timing_rows <- function(m, rows, s) {  # the window moved back month by month, on the dead cells and as many live cells
  rows <- c(rows[samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1], sample(rows[samples$dead[rows] == 0], sum(samples$dead[rows] >= 0.1)))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(ym[window:length(ym)], function(e) { w <- series(e, 1L, rows); w$dates <- s$dates  # sits reads the steps by position
    data.frame(samples[rows, c("roi", "set", "dead")], end = e, p_dead = p_dead(m, rows, w)) }))
}
if (!file.exists(pred_csv)) {
  torch::torch_manual_seed(20260915); preds <- list(); timing <- list()
  for (k in intervals) {
    s <- series("202108", k)
    for (f in 1:5) { m <- fit(which(train & use & samples$fold != f), s); te <- which(train & complete & samples$fold == f)
      preds[[length(preds) + 1]] <- score_rows(m, te, s, k); if (k == 1L) timing[[length(timing) + 1]] <- timing_rows(m, te, s) }
    m <- fit(which(train & use), s); te <- which(!train & complete)
    preds[[length(preds) + 1]] <- score_rows(m, te, s, k); if (k == 1L) timing[[length(timing) + 1]] <- timing_rows(m, te, s)
  }
  write.csv(do.call(rbind, preds), pred_csv, row.names = FALSE); write.csv(do.call(rbind, timing), timing_csv, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

The network was the temporal convolutional network of @Pelletier_2019 as implemented in the sits package [@Simoes_2021], three one-dimensional convolutional layers of 64 filters with a kernel of three steps, batch normalisation, a rectified linear unit and dropout of 0.2 after each, then a dense layer of 256 units with dropout of 0.5 and a softmax over the two classes, trained with the AdamW optimiser at a learning rate of 0.0005 on the four bands after the quantile scaling that sits applies to every band. Each network was trained for at most 60 epochs on at most 10,000 cells per class drawn at random from its training areas, with a fifth of them held back to stop training once validation loss had not improved by 0.01 for 10 epochs. A cell was classed as dead when the network gave that class a probability of 0.5 or more. To reconstruct the timing of detection, the monthly network of each fold was applied to the same 24-month window ending in every month from May 2019 to August 2021, on every dead cell of its held-out areas and as many live cells drawn at random, so that the share of cells detected as dead could be traced back through the record.

## Accuracy assessment

```{r}
#| label: accuracy
#| echo: true
#| output: false
pred <- read.csv(pred_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character")); pred$label <- pred$dead >= 0.1; pred$hit <- pred$p_dead >= 0.5
auc <- function(x, y) { r <- rank(x); n1 <- sum(y); (sum(r[y]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * (length(y) - n1)) }
score <- function(d) { d <- d[d$label | d$dead == 0, ]; tp <- sum(d$hit & d$label)
  c(precision = tp / sum(d$hit), recall = tp / sum(d$label), F1 = 2 * tp / (sum(d$hit) + sum(d$label)), AUC = auc(d$p_dead, d$label)) }
acc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pred, list(pred$interval, pred$set)), function(d) data.frame(set = d$set[1], interval = d$interval[1], t(score(d)))))
acc <- acc[order(acc$set == "test", acc$interval), ]
bins <- c(-1, 0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1); bin_names <- c("None", "Edge only (0 to 0.1)", "0.1 to 0.25", "0.25 to 0.5", "0.5 to 1")
pred$bin <- cut(pred$dead, bins, bin_names)
floor_tbl <- with(pred[pred$set == "training", ], tapply(hit, list(bin, interval), mean))
floor_n <- with(pred[pred$set == "training" & pred$interval == 1, ], table(bin))
tm <- read.csv(timing_csv, colClasses = c(roi = "character", end = "character")); tm$hit <- tm$p_dead >= 0.5
timing <- aggregate(hit ~ end + set + label, transform(tm, label = ifelse(dead >= 0.1, "Dead by August 2021", "No dead crown")), mean)
timing$date <- as.Date(paste0(timing$end, "01"), "%Y%m%d")
j <- (match("202108", ym) - window + 1):match("202108", ym)  # one band averaged over the same window, with no training, for comparison
base_auc <- sapply(c(training = TRUE, test = FALSE), function(tr) sapply(bands, function(b) auc(rowMeans(cube[train == tr & use, j, b]), samples$dead[train == tr & use] >= 0.1)))
acc_csv <- "03.outputs/accuracy.csv"  # read by the abstract-numbers chunk at the head of the next render
write.csv(rbind(data.frame(method = "TempCNN", acc), data.frame(method = "One-band mean", set = colnames(base_auc), interval = NA, precision = NA, recall = NA, F1 = NA, AUC = apply(base_auc, 2, max))), acc_csv, row.names = FALSE)
ads_year <- data.frame(year = 2016:2024, ha = sapply(2016:2024, function(y) sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(ads[ads$SURVEY_YEAR == y, ]))) / 1e4))
```

Precision, recall, F1 score and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were computed between the network's class and the crown label over the held-out cells of the five folds pooled, and separately over the test areas, for each compositing interval. For comparison, the mean of each band over the same 24 months was scored on its own, with no training, by the area under the curve it gave over the same cells. The share of cells classed as dead was then tabulated by the dead crown fraction of the cell, including the edge-only cells and the cells with no crown, so that the lowest fraction at which the radar detected mortality could be read against the false detection rate on cells with none. The timing reconstruction was summarised as the share of dead cells and of live cells detected in each window, and set against the area of spruce beetle damage the aerial detection survey mapped in the frame of @fig-study in each year.

# Results

## Sampled record

```{r}
#| label: fig-series
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Mean monthly slope-corrected backscatter of the four bands, June 2017 to August 2021, over the cells labelled dead (dead crown fraction of 0.1 or more) and alive (no dead crown) on 2 August 2021, all label areas pooled."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5
prof <- do.call(rbind, lapply(bands, function(b) do.call(rbind, lapply(c(dead = TRUE, alive = FALSE), function(lab) data.frame(
  band = b, class = if (lab) "Dead" else "Alive", date = months, dB = colMeans(cube[use & (samples$dead >= 0.1) == lab, , b], na.rm = TRUE))))))
ggplot(prof, aes(date, dB, colour = class)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) + facet_wrap(~band, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Backscatter (dB)", colour = NULL) + th
```

Of the `r format(nrow(cells), big.mark = ",")` cells, `r format(nrow(samples), big.mark = ",")` were sampled from Earth Engine and `r format(sum(complete), big.mark = ",")` carried a complete series after interpolation, over `r months_seen[1]` months of the ascending orbit and `r months_seen[2]` of the descending orbit. `r format(sum(use & train & samples$dead >= 0.1), big.mark = ",")` training cells and `r format(sum(use & !train & samples$dead >= 0.1), big.mark = ",")` test cells were labelled dead, against `r format(sum(use & train & samples$dead == 0), big.mark = ",")` and `r format(sum(use & !train & samples$dead == 0), big.mark = ",")` labelled alive. Over the whole record the mean VH backscatter of the dead cells differed from that of the live cells by `r sprintf("%+.2f", mean(cube[use & samples$dead >= 0.1, , "VH131"]) - mean(cube[use & samples$dead == 0, , "VH131"]))` dB on the descending orbit and `r sprintf("%+.2f", mean(cube[use & samples$dead >= 0.1, , "VH65"]) - mean(cube[use & samples$dead == 0, , "VH65"]))` dB on the ascending orbit, the dead cells being the `r ifelse(mean(cube[use & samples$dead >= 0.1, , "VH131"]) > mean(cube[use & samples$dead == 0, , "VH131"]), "brighter", "darker")`, and the seasonal cycle of both classes was dominated by the winter fall of backscatter over frozen ground (@fig-series).

## Accuracy by interval

```{r}
#| label: tbl-accuracy
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement of the network's class with the crown label at the held-out cells of the five spatial folds and at the independent test areas, by compositing interval, for cells with a dead crown fraction of 0.1 or more against cells with none."
fmt_tbl(data.frame(Areas = ifelse(acc$set == "training", "Held-out folds", "Test areas"), `Interval (months)` = acc$interval,
                   round(acc[, c("precision", "recall", "F1", "AUC")], 2), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL) |>
          setNames(c("Areas", "Interval (months)", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "AUC")))
```

```{r}
#| label: acc-text
#| echo: true
#| output: false
best <- acc[acc$set == "training", ][which.max(acc$F1[acc$set == "training"]), ]; worst <- acc[acc$set == "training", ][which.min(acc$F1[acc$set == "training"]), ]
tb <- acc[acc$set == "test", ]; tbest <- tb[which.max(tb$F1), ]
```

On the held-out folds the network separated dead from live cells with an F1 score of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$F1)` at the `r best$interval`-month interval, the highest of the four intervals, against `r sprintf("%.2f", worst$F1)` at the `r worst$interval`-month interval, the lowest, and the area under the curve ran from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(acc$AUC[acc$set == "training"]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(acc$AUC[acc$set == "training"]))` (@tbl-accuracy). Dead cells made up `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(pred$label[pred$set == "training" & pred$interval == 1 & (pred$label | pred$dead == 0)]))` per cent of the held-out cells, so a precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$precision)` is the share a random draw would give. On the test areas of @Zwieback_2024 the network classed `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(pred$hit[pred$set == "test" & pred$interval == 1]))` per cent of cells as dead at the monthly interval, and its F1 score was highest at the `r tbest$interval`-month interval, `r sprintf("%.2f", tbest$F1)`, with a precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", tbest$precision)` and a recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", tbest$recall)`. The mean of a single band over the same 24 months, with no training, ranked dead cells above live cells with an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", min(base_auc[, "training"]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(base_auc[, "training"]))` over the training cells and `r sprintf("%.2f", min(base_auc[, "test"]))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(base_auc[, "test"]))` over the test cells, the highest in each case being `r rownames(base_auc)[which.max(base_auc[, "training"])]` and `r rownames(base_auc)[which.max(base_auc[, "test"])]`.

## Detectability floor

```{r}
#| label: tbl-floor
#| echo: true
#| tbl-cap: "Share of held-out training cells classed as dead by the network, by the fraction of the cell covered by dead crowns on 2 August 2021 and by compositing interval; the first row is the false detection rate on cells with no dead crown."
fmt_tbl(data.frame(`Dead crown fraction` = rownames(floor_tbl), Cells = format(as.integer(floor_n), big.mark = ","), round(floor_tbl, 2), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL) |>
          setNames(c("Dead crown fraction", "Cells", paste(colnames(floor_tbl), "months"))))
```

At the monthly interval the network classed `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["0.5 to 1", "1"])` per cent of the held-out cells more than half covered by dead crowns as dead, `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["0.25 to 0.5", "1"])` per cent of those covered between a quarter and a half, and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["0.1 to 0.25", "1"])` per cent of those covered between a tenth and a quarter, about one crown, against `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["None", "1"])` per cent of the cells with no dead crown and `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["Edge only (0 to 0.1)", "1"])` per cent of those touched only by the edge of a crown (@tbl-floor).

## Timing of detection

```{r}
#| label: fig-timing
#| echo: true
#| fig-cap: "Share of held-out cells classed as dead by the monthly network as its 24-month window was moved back through the record, for cells with a dead crown fraction of 0.1 or more on 2 August 2021 and for cells with none, on the training folds and the test areas (top), and the area of spruce beetle damage mapped by the aerial detection survey in the frame of Figure 1 in each year (bottom)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
top <- ggplot(timing, aes(date, hit, colour = label, linetype = ifelse(set == "training", "Held-out folds", "Test areas"))) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + labs(x = "End of the 24-month window", y = "Cells classed dead", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) + th
bottom <- ggplot(ads_year, aes(factor(year), ha / 1000)) + geom_col(fill = "grey40") + labs(x = "Survey year", y = "Damage mapped (kha)") + th
top / bottom + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(3, 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: timing-text
#| echo: true
#| output: false
tt <- timing[timing$set == "training" & timing$label == "Dead by August 2021", ]; tf <- timing[timing$set == "training" & timing$label == "No dead crown", ]
peak <- tt$end[order(-tt$hit)][1:4]
```

The share of cells classed as dead followed the month in which the window ended and not the label. In the window ending August 2021 the network classed `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * tt$hit[tt$end == "202108"])` per cent of the held-out cells dead by that date as dead, against `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * tf$hit[tf$end == "202108"])` per cent of the cells with no dead crown, and in no earlier window did it class more than `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * max(tt$hit[tt$end != "202108"]))` per cent of the dead cells as dead (@fig-timing). The two shares rose and fell together across the `r nrow(tt)` windows, with a correlation of `r sprintf("%.2f", cor(tt$hit, tf$hit))`, and the four windows with the most detections ended in `r sub(",([^,]+)$", " and\\1", paste(format(as.Date(paste0(sort(peak), "01"), "%Y%m%d"), "%B %Y"), collapse = ", "))`. The aerial detection survey mapped the largest area of spruce beetle damage in the frame of @fig-study in `r ads_year$year[which.max(ads_year$ha)]`, `r format(round(max(ads_year$ha)), big.mark = ",")` ha, and none in 2020.

# Discussion

Over the Susitna valley label areas of @Zwieback_2024, the Sentinel-1 record of June 2017 to August 2021 and the temporal convolutional network did not separate 10 m cells holding dead spruce crowns from cells holding none on areas the network had not seen. On the five held-out folds the F1 score stayed between `r sprintf("%.2f", min(acc$F1[acc$set == "training"]))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", max(acc$F1[acc$set == "training"]))` at every compositing interval, precision equalled the share of dead cells in the sample, and the area under the curve stayed below `r sprintf("%.2f", max(acc$AUC[acc$set == "training"]))`, while on the independent test areas the monthly network classed almost every cell as alive. The mean of one band over the same window, with no training, ranked the cells better than the network did, so the network added nothing to the radar and lost part of what the radar carried. The first objective, accuracy by interval, therefore has the answer that no interval from one to six months gave a usable map, and the second, the detectability floor, has the answer that the network classed cells more than half covered by dead crowns as dead only `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["0.5 to 1", "1"])` per cent of the time against a false detection rate of `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * floor_tbl["None", "1"])` per cent, so no fraction was detected at an operating point that a map could use. This stands against the variance explained by @Hechtl_2025 in Bavaria, which was measured on pixels split at random within polygons, and it is the first measure of the radar on beetle-killed spruce over areas held out whole.

Three features of the design explain much of the result, and each is a decision rather than a property of the radar. The live class was every cell without a dead crown, which in areas that @Zwieback_2024 selected "with the goal of covering a spectrum of land cover types (including areas without trees)" [@Zwieback_2024, p. 414] includes wetland, floodplain and treeless ground whose backscatter sits well below that of a spruce canopy, and the `r sprintf("%.1f", abs(mean(cube[use & samples$dead >= 0.1, , "VH131"]) - mean(cube[use & samples$dead == 0, , "VH131"])))` dB by which the dead cells outshone the live cells on the descending orbit is the signature of that mixture, not of mortality, so the network had land cover to learn and learned it, and land cover differs between folds. The 10 m cell is the scale of one crown, and a monthly median of two or three scenes after a 3 by 3 mean still carries speckle of the order of the signal that one dead crown can give in a mixed stand of 10 to 30 per cent conifer, where the volume scattering of the surrounding canopy dominates the cell; @Zwieback_2024 defined severity at the 90 m stand scale for that reason. The labels carry one date, and a crown dead on 2 August 2021 may have died before June 2017, so for many cells the window held no change to detect, only a state, and at C-band a dead crown standing in a living canopy differs little from its neighbours. The `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * gaps)` per cent of monthly values that were interpolated and the loss of `r format(nrow(cells) - nrow(samples), big.mark = ",")` cells to layover and shadow masking are minor beside these.

The timing reconstruction showed what the network had learned. Every fold's network classed most cells as dead only when the window ended in August 2021, the month its training window ended, and the share it classed as dead in the other windows rose and fell identically for cells with and without dead crowns, so the network had fitted the position of the seasonal cycle within the window rather than any change in the cells. Nothing about when the mortality became detectable can be read from that, and the question that motivated the study, whether the radar can date emergent mortality closely enough to time trap placement, remains open rather than answered in the negative, because a network that has not learned mortality cannot be asked when it appeared.

The next design follows from the three decisions. The live class should be living forest, cells with conifer cover and no dead crown, so that the contrast is mortality alone; the unit should be the 30 or 90 m stand cell at which @Zwieback_2024 reported severity, with the radar averaged over it, so that speckle falls below the signal; and the record should begin before the outbreak reached the area, which on the descending orbit means the scenes of 2016, so that the window holds the change and not only the state. The one-band comparison shows that a signal exists at the pooled scale, an area under the curve of `r sprintf("%.2f", max(base_auc[, "training"]))` from the mean of one band, and whether a network trained on those labels can turn it into a map at a monthly interval is the test this study did not yet make.

# Conclusion

Trained on the dead spruce crowns of @Zwieback_2024 and the slope-corrected Sentinel-1 record of June 2017 to August 2021, a temporal convolutional network did not separate 10 m cells holding dead crowns from cells holding none on label areas held out whole, at monthly, two-monthly, quarterly or half-yearly intervals, and the mean of one band over the same window ranked the cells better than the network. The network learned the land cover mixed into the live class and the season at which its window ended, so no detectability floor and no timing of detection could be read from it. The reference data and the radar record support a second design, living forest against dead at the stand scale with a record that starts before the outbreak, and that design is the one on which the monthly question should be put.

## Data availability

All inputs were publicly available and were read by the code shown in this manuscript. The crown labels of @Zwieback_2024 were downloaded from Zenodo under the licence given in the code, the Sentinel-1 ground range detected scenes and the Copernicus 30 m digital elevation model were read in Google Earth Engine under the asset names given in the code, the aerial detection survey damage areas were downloaded from the United States Forest Service, and the state boundary from the United States Census Bureau. The dead crown fraction and sampled backscatter of each cell, the fold predictions and the tables and figures are held with the manuscript under `02.inputs/derived` and `03.outputs`, and every number in the text is computed from them at render time.
